characters.summary: Tulkas is the champion of the Valar, fighting purely with his bare hands, immense physical strength, and unyielding speed. He requires no weapons or mounts and wrestled Melkor into submission during the days before the shaping of Arda.

mechanisms: Invulnerability to cold, heat, and standard physical trauma by virtue of divine nature

weaknesses: Laughter and mirth can sometimes lead to an underestimation of subtle deception
limitations: Fights entirely without weapons or armor
Cannot run down every hidden evil if they conceal themselves deeply in deception

sources.supports: Basic attributes, role as champion of the Valar, and wrestling Melkor.

feats.claim: Laughed and wrestled Melkor to the ground single-handedly during the Battle of the Powers.

notableResults.note: Subdued Melkor in hand-to-hand combat during the assault on Utumno

unknowns: Exact limits of his physical strength before exhaustion in prolonged divine combat

characters.summary: Tuor is a mortal hero of the Edain, guided by the Vala Ulmo to the hidden city of Gondolin. He wields the axe Dramborleg and fights with exceptional skill, later being granted immortality among the Eldar.

mechanisms: Divine protection and omens from Ulmo

weaknesses: Mortal vulnerability to standard physical injuries and fatigue
mobility: Travels primarily on foot and by boat
limitations: Mortal limitations in stamina and vulnerability until his transition to the kindred of the Eldar

sources.supports: Lineage, journey to Gondolin, and association with Ulmo.

feats.claim: Slew several Orcs and a Balrog during the Fall of Gondolin.
feats.citation: The Fall of Gondolin (Unfinished Tales / The Book of Lost Tales)

campaignTags.claim: Possesses a deep natural affinity for the sea granted by Ulmo and swims exceptionally well.

unknowns: The exact manner of his final departure into the West beyond Valinor

characters.summary: Turgon is the Elven King of Gondolin, ruling a hidden realm of master craftsmen and warriors. He wields the sword Glamdring and directs his defenses from behind the formidable mountain barriers of the Encircling Mountains.

mechanisms: The impenetrable geography and fortifications of Gondolin

weaknesses: Prone to isolationism and over-reliance on secrecy, leaving the realm vulnerable to internal betrayal
mobility: Standard Elven mobility on foot and horseback
limitations: Bound to the defense of his city rather than mobile offensive campaigns

sources.supports: Rule of Gondolin, wielding Glamdring, and fate during the fall of the city.

feats.claim: Established and ruled the hidden city of Gondolin for centuries.

notableResults.note: Gondolin fell due to betrayal and siege engines

unknowns: Direct combat feats prior to the sack of Gondolin

characters.continuity: The Silmarillion and The Children of Húrin
characters.summary: Túrin is a tragic and fiercely skilled human warrior of the House of Hador. Armed with the black-iron sword Gurthang, he fights with devastating martial prowess and indomitable will, though pursued by the curse of Morgoth.

mechanisms: Heavy plate armor and dragon-helm of Hador
Exceptional pain tolerance and psychological resilience against despair

weaknesses: Susceptible to deception, pride, and the active curse of Morgoth affecting his judgment
limitations: Prone to tragic miscalculations driven by curse-induced misfortune

sources.supports: Wielding Gurthang, slaying Glaurung, and tragic fate.

feats.claim: Slew the great dragon Glaurung by stabbing him from beneath with Gurthang.
Led outlaw bands in the wilderness of Dorthonion and Brethil successfully.

notableResults.note: Mortally wounded the dragon at Cabed Naeramarth
Inadvertently killed his closest friend under a deluding spell of Morgoth

unknowns: The exact metaphysical mechanics of Morgoth's curse upon his mind

characters.summary: Uglúk is a fierce Uruk-hai captain serving Saruman. He leads a brutal cohort of crossbred orcs across Rohan with harsh discipline, carrying captives Merry and Pippin toward Isengard.

techniques: Intimidation and command of subordinate orcs

mechanisms: Thick Uruk hide and high pain tolerance

weaknesses: Arrogance and lack of tactical flexibility against mounted cavalry
limitations: Limited to standard physical weapons and infantry tactics

sources.supports: Role as Uruk-hai captain, leadership of the raiding party, and death by Éomer.

feats.claim: Beheaded Grishnákh and enforced forced marches across Rohan without rest.

notableResults.citation: The Two Towers, 'The Riders of Rohan'
notableResults.note: Slain in single combat by Éomer during the ambush of the Uruk band

unknowns: Exact origins before being bred in the pits of Isengard

characters.summary: Ulmo is one of the Aratar, the Lord of Waters and second in might among the Valar. He operates largely unseen beneath the oceans and rivers, communicating through visions, music of the water, and direct interventions on behalf of Elves and Men.
mobility: Omnipresent within the global hydrological cycle of Arda
limitations: Obeys Eru Ilúvatar and acts mostly through counsel rather than direct physical rule from Valinor

sources.supports: Status as one of the Valar, Lord of Waters, and independent protector of Middle-earth inhabitants.

feats.claim: Raised the Vale of Tumladen and guided Tuor to Gondolin.
Struck terror into the hearts of the hosts of Valinor with his terrifying aquatic manifestation.

notableResults.note: Maintained hidden pockets of resistance and thwarted Melkor's designs via water-borne interventions

campaignTags.claim: Absolute dominion over all waters, oceans, and rivers of Arda.
Can manipulate global waters, raise massive waves, and shape river courses.

unknowns: Full extent of his power relative to Manwë outside the element of water

characters.summary: Ungoliant is a primordial spirit of monstrous spider form who hungers for all light, consuming it to weave webs of impenetrable darkness. She fights by draining energy and light with her webs and venom, and grew to colossal proportions after devouring the Two Trees of Valinor.

techniques: Unlight webs to blind and suffocate opponents

mechanisms: Cloak of Unlight (absolute darkness that blocks vision and magic)

weaknesses: Insatiable hunger that can drive her to consume herself if left unfed
Overwhelming radiant light of the Valar
limitations: Power depends directly on consuming light or energy; weakens without sustenance

sources.supports: Primeval nature, association with spiders and darkness, and destruction of the Two Trees.

feats.claim: Drained the Two Trees of Valinor of all sap and life, plunging Valinor into darkness.
Bound and nearly consumed Morgoth in her webs before his Balrogs rescued him.

notableResults.note: Overpowered Morgoth when he refused to hand over the Silmarils, forcing Balrogs to intervene
Driven off only by the combined flames of multiple Balrogs wielding whips

campaignTags.claim: Grew to monstrous, towering proportions after consuming the light of the Two Trees.
Weaves a cloak of Unlight that plunges surroundings into absolute darkness for concealment.

unknowns: Her exact ultimate fate after fleeing into the southern wastes of Middle-earth

characters.summary: Vairë the Weaver is one of the Valier, weaving all things that ever were in Time into her ever-expanding tapestries that fill the halls of Mandos. Her power is conceptual and temporal rather than combat-oriented.

techniques: Weaving the tapestry of Time and fate
Recording all history within her looms

mechanisms: Divine invulnerability within the halls of Valinor

weaknesses: Not established in direct combat contexts
mobility: Standard divine teleportation and movement within Valinor
limitations: Confined to her duties in the Halls of Mandos and does not engage in physical warfare

sources.supports: Listing of Vairë as one of the Valier and wife of Mandos, known as the Weaver.

feats.claim: Wove the entire history and timeline of Arda into the tapestries of Mandos.

unknowns: Any direct offensive capabilities outside her dominion over time-tapestries

characters.summary: Vána the Ever-young is one of the Valier, sister of Yavanna and spouse of Oromë. Flowers spring up and birds sing wherever she walks, and her power centers on the rejuvenation and blossoming of nature.

mechanisms: Divine resilience and immunity to ordinary harm

weaknesses: Not established in direct combat contexts
limitations: Does not participate in martial conflicts or physical combat

sources.supports: Listing of Vána as one of the Valier, associated with youth, flowers, and nature.

feats.claim: Maintained eternal springtime and gardens filled with golden flowers in Valinor.

campaignTags.claim: Possesses divine capacity to restore life and flourishing vitality to flora and fauna.

unknowns: Extent of defensive abilities if directly attacked
